name: Oude Geuze
research: Flagship gueuze from Brouwerij 3 Fonteinen. A blend of 1-, 2-, and 3-year-old lambics, unfiltered and unpasteurized, bottle-conditioned for at least 6 months. Spontaneous fermentation with wild yeasts, matured in oak casks. Aromas evolve from vibrant citrus and grassy notes to mellow oak and stone fruit with age. Can be cellared for several decades. Untappd: 4.05/5 (80,000+ ratings). https://untappd.com/b/brouwerij-3-fonteinen-3-fonteinen-oude-geuze/4009
food_pairings: Aged cheeses, oysters, mussels, charcuterie, lemon-dressed seafood
considerations: Bottled 26 Nov 2018. Best before 26 Oct 2038 (printed on bottle). No two bottlings are alike. Cellared properly, this bottle has 12+ years of drinking window remaining.

name: Oude Geuze Cuvee Armand & Gaston
research:
Untappd: blend of 1-, 2-, and 3-year-old traditional lambics from the 2018 season. Spontaneous fermentation, unfiltered and unpasteurized. Named after founders Armand Debelder and Gaston Debelder. 3 Fonteinen notes "no two bottlings are alike" due to barrel selection variables.

Rating: 4.3/5 (32,202 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brouwerij-3-fonteinen-3-fonteinen-oude-geuze-cuvee-armand-gaston/1594814)
food_pairings: Mussels, oysters, aged Gouda, charcuterie. Classic gueuze pairing — acidity cuts through rich and fatty foods.
considerations: Based on 2018-season lambics — likely bottled 2019-2020, now 6-7 years post-bottle. Probably at or near peak. "Steadfast adherence to tradition" per 3F. One of the most-rated gueuzes on Untappd.

name: Langste Nacht 2019 | Karwijzaad Op Het Koelschip
research:
Untappd: experimental lambic macerated with caraway seeds on the coolship during the "Longest Night" (2019 harvest). Part of 3 Fonteinen's "Speling van het Lot" (Twist of Fate) small-batch experimental series. Bottled April 13, 2021 with ~12 months weighted average age. One quarter of cereals from the Pajottenland region.

Full Untappd name: SvhL XIV.iii Langste Nacht 2019 | Karwijzaad Op Het Koelschip
Rating: 4.19/5 (505 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brouwerij-3-fonteinen-svhl-xiv-iii-langste-nacht-2019-karwijzaad-op-het-koelschip/4805170)
food_pairings: Caraway rye bread, aged Edam, light smoked fish. Caraway spice bridges well with savory herbal flavors.
considerations: "Speling van het Lot" (Twist of Fate) series — extremely limited, experimental. Bottled April 2021 from 2019 harvest. Now ~5 years post-bottle. The caraway seed character (similar to rye bread spice) is distinctive. No longer in production.

name: Tete de Cuvee
research:
Untappd: complex vintage blend — 36% Oude du Ble (16 months in 225L French oak barrels) plus five separate batches of Oude Fermier aged 12-25 months in various French oak vessels. Described as fruit-forward with "sweet nectarine" notes and slight tartness.

Rating: 4.39/5 (1,585 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/side-project-brewing-tete-de-cuvee-vintage-2022/5569618)
food_pairings: Stone fruit desserts, mild aged cheeses, light poultry. The nectarine and stone fruit notes complement delicate flavors.
considerations: Side Project's flagship blend — very highly rated (top 5% on Untappd). Complex multi-component blend from 2022 vintage. Now ~3-4 years post-release, well into its window. No longer in production.

name: Oude Fermier
research:
Untappd: farmhouse ale / saison in the Belgian tradition. The Oude Fermier series is Side Project's flagship Belgian-inspired farmhouse program — multi-barrel blends aged in French oak. The 2022 vintage is rated 4.39/5.

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/side-project-brewing-oude-fermier-vintage-2022/5675248)
food_pairings: Roast chicken, Gruyere, fresh herbs, grilled white fish.
considerations: Side Project is a St. Louis farmhouse brewery revered for Belgian-inspired ales. Oude Fermier is their best-known beer. The 2022 vintage is now ~3-4 years old and well into its window. No longer in production.

name: MMXXI Muscat
research:
Farmhouse ale / saison primary fermented on native-fermented Muscat grapes from Palimpsest Vineyard, Newberg, OR. Grape harvest: Sep 25, 2021. Bottled: Mar 3, 2022 with raw honey from Cougar Canyon Apiary.

No official brewer drink window published. Drink window (2024-03-01 to 2027-03-01) is my recommendation based on:
- Comparable MMXXI-series Floodland releases (Rhone, No Echoes)
- Muscat aromatics (rose, orange blossom, stone fruit) are most expressive at 2-4 years post-bottling; brett character continues developing
- Untappd check-ins from 2024-2025 describe it as "smooth, grape peel, light funk" -- still tracking well at 4 years
- ABV 7.44% supports extended cellaring vs. lighter Floodland releases

Sources:
[Untappd - MMXXI Muscat (2021)](https://untappd.com/b/floodland-brewing-mmxxi-muscat-2021/4953395)
[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
food_pairings: Fresh goat cheese or burrata, stone fruit (peach, apricot, nectarine), lightly spiced dishes (Thai, Vietnamese, Moroccan), grilled fish, crème brûlée or tarte tatin
considerations: Bottle conditioned with raw honey -- expect light sediment, store upright. Grapes from Palimpsest Vineyard (Newberg, OR); honey from Cougar Canyon Apiary. No longer in production. Rated 4.39/5 on Untappd (366 ratings).

name: The Unblended Armagandias
research:
Untappd: spontaneous wild ale aged 2 years in oak Armagnac barrels, bottled March 2021 ("3/21" Premier Keeper Bottle). De Garde spontaneous ales typically peak 3-8 years post-bottling; Armagnac barrel character integrates beautifully with extended age.

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/de-garde-brewing-the-unblended-armagandias/4434932)
food_pairings: Aged cheeses, charcuterie, duck confit. The Armagnac barrel notes pair well with rich, fatty foods.
considerations: "3/21" in the name refers to the March 2021 bottling date. Now ~5 years post-bottle — likely in prime drinking window. Described as tart and dry with vinous, wine-like qualities and Armagnac barrel notes. No longer in production.

name: The Vintage
research:
Untappd: spontaneous wild ale aged 4 years in oak barrels before bottling May 2022 — an exclusive Keepers Bottle release. Four years of oak aging gives exceptional depth and stability. Now ~4 years post-bottle; well into its drinking window.

Rating: 4.09/5 (315 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/de-garde-brewing-the-vintage-2018/5152046)
food_pairings: Farmhouse cheeses, roast chicken, mushroom dishes, light charcuterie.
considerations: Quantity ×2. A premium De Garde release — "The Vintage" series represents best-of-year barrels selected by the brewery. Bottled May 2022 after 4 years of aging, meaning this contains 2018 harvest lambic. No longer in production.

name: Sen XXVI
research:
Single wort spelt wheat saison. Open fermented in stainless (May 2023), then aged 15 months in neutral oak barrels before bottling. Whole flower Crystal hops from Kirk family, Willamette Valley Farms. Bottle conditioned with organic sugar.

Brewer Adam Paysse note (from Floodland bottle log): "Drinking great now, will continue to do so for some time. I imagine this will evolve in the bottle, best before Spring 2028."

Flavor profile: balanced acidity and bitterness, distinct Brett character that remains bright and aromatic, floral with orange-leaning citrus from Crystal hops.

Sources:
[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log - Sen XXVI](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
[Sen XXVI Review - rihobeer.com](https://rihobeer.com/en/floodland-brewing-sen-xxvi-artisanal-saison-combining-water-like-mouthfeel-with-complex-fermentation-aromas/)
food_pairings: Soft-rind cheeses (Brie, Camembert), raw oysters or shellfish, roast chicken, spring vegetables, stone fruit desserts
considerations: "Sen" = Senescence; XXVI means this is the 26th in the series. Bottle conditioned with organic sugar. Bright, floral Brett character will soften and integrate further over the aging window. ABV 6.37%.

name: MMXXIV Gruner Veltliner
research:
Floodland Bottle Log (Adam Paysse): bottled 01/16/2025, ABV 8.29%. "Best by summer 2027. Drink best next 18 months."

[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
considerations: Higher ABV Floodland blend. Adam Paysse notes best within 18 months of bottling (i.e., by ~July 2026), though summer 2027 is the outer limit.

name: Nothing Ever Begins
research:
Floodland Bottle Log (Adam Paysse): bottled 04/24/2025, ABV 6.99%. "Best before spring 2027. Drink fresh."

[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
considerations: Relatively short window per Adam Paysse — drink before spring 2027. No extended aging benefit.

name: I Want to Be Known
research:
Floodland Bottle Log (Adam Paysse): bottled 05/29/2025, ABV 4.89%. "Best before fall 2028. Drink fresh."

[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
considerations: A lighter Floodland release. Adam Paysse recommends drinking fresh — no extended aging benefit. Drink before fall 2028.

name: MMXXIII/MMXXIV True-Nature
research:
From Untappd / Floodland: blend of biodynamic Kerner grape pomace, organic Balaton cherries, and organic red raspberries from the 2023-2024 harvests. Refermented in bottle with organic cane sugar. Bottled 06/12/2025. Best consumed before summer 2027.

[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
considerations: Untappd community Gold Award 2026. Named after Ursula K. LeGuin quote. Your beers.md listed this as MMXXII/MMXXIv — Untappd confirms the blend is 2023/2024 vintages.

name: MMXXIV Flowers of the Field
research:
Farmhouse ale with entirely native fermentation of Chardonnay grapes (French Creek Vineyard, Yakima River Valley) and Pinot Noir grapes (Johan Vineyards, Van Duzer Corridor), 2024 harvest. Blended open and barrel-fermented saison. Bottle conditioned with organic sugar.

Brewer note: "Conditioned in the bottle for 6+ months prior to release and is drinking great. It should continue to drink well for several years, but I don't think aging will improve it. Best before 2029."

Sources:
[Untappd - MMXXIV Flowers of the Field](https://untappd.com/b/floodland-brewing-mmxxiv-flowers-of-the-field-2024-harvest/6641152)
[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
food_pairings: Brie and triple-crème cheeses, roast salmon, spring pea dishes, herb-roasted chicken, white peach tart
considerations: Brewer explicitly states aging will NOT improve this beer — drink it now through 2028. The Chardonnay and Pinot Noir grape blend gives this a wine-like character. French Creek Vineyard (Yakima) + Johan Vineyards (Van Duzer Corridor, OR) are both highly regarded sources for Floodland.

name: Monarchist
research:
Floodland Bottle Log (Adam Paysse): bottled 10/31/2024, ABV 6.12%. "Will improve the next 12+ months." Best before fall 2028.

[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
considerations: A Floodland flagship blend. Adam Paysse notes continued improvement through at least October 2025, peaking before fall 2028.

name: Vesper
research: Table beer from Holy Mountain Brewing (Seattle, WA). Pilsner malt, flaked rye and wheat; hopped with Styrian Golding and Cascade; fermented with Belgian yeast and conditioned with Brettanomyces. Low-ABV but complex — the Brett adds earthy, funky depth. Won Silver in 2026 Untappd Community Awards. No 2025-specific Untappd listing; current bottlings are logged to the base entry. https://untappd.com/b/holy-mountain-brewing-vesper/2515677
food_pairings: Light charcuterie, soft cheeses, roast chicken, grain salads
considerations: 2025 bottling, likely summer. Exact bottle date unknown — estimated July 2025. Brett-conditioned table beer; drink young to fresh but will develop further over 2-3 years. 2 bottles in cellar.

name: Cherry Field Blend
research:
Oak-fermented farmhouse saison refermented on foraged Cornelian cherries, organic Balaton, Montmorency, and Van cherries. Bottle conditioned with organic cane sugar.

Brewer note (Untappd): "Field Blend is an exercise in embracing time as a source of wonder rather than an instrument of control." Best before summer 2028.

Note: The 2024 Cherry Field Blend (bottled Oct 2024) had a best-before of early 2027 — this 2025 bottling extends that window to summer 2028.

Sources:
[Untappd - Cherry Field Blend (2025)](https://untappd.com/b/floodland-brewing-cherry-field-blend-2025/6641153)
[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
food_pairings: Aged gouda or comté, duck with cherry sauce, lamb chops, dark chocolate tart, charcuterie with sour cherry preserves
considerations: Bottle conditioned — expect light sediment. Four cherry varieties: Cornelian (foraged), Balaton, Montmorency, Van. The cherry character in Floodland Field Blends tends to integrate and deepen with age rather than fade. Drinking great now and through summer 2028.

name: Temps & Poivre
research:
Untappd: "A Spontaneous Wild Ale with Black Pepper Aged in Oak Barrels for Six Years. Bottled 11/24 Premier Keeper Bottle." Six years of oak aging predates bottling — the base lambic is highly developed. Black pepper integrates well with extended time. Allow at least 12 months of bottle rest.

Rating: 4.28/5 (98 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/de-garde-brewing-temps-poivre-11-24/6194067)
food_pairings: Spiced meat dishes, aged gouda, dark chocolate, roasted vegetables.
considerations: "11/24" in the name denotes the November 2024 bottling. Despite 6 years of barrel aging, bottle conditioning benefits from at least 1 year of rest before opening. The black pepper spice character is "well-integrated" per reviewers.

name: Between Two Toms
research:
Untappd: spontaneous wild ale with chamomile flowers, aged in oak gin barrels 2-4 years, then blended with Voodoo Brewing. "Moderate acidity, but the botanicals and chamomile are poppin." A collaboration beer — unusual gin barrel provenance gives it distinct botanical character.

Rating: 4.17/5 (33 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/de-garde-brewing-between-two-toms/6458919)
food_pairings: Light seafood, soft cheeses, cucumber dishes. The chamomile and gin botanicals work with delicate flavors.
considerations: Collaboration with Voodoo Brewing. The gin barrel origin is unusual for a wild ale — expect juniper and botanical notes alongside the spontaneous funk. Relatively recent release with limited check-ins.

name: Ill Fate
research:
Blended saison refermented on organic red raspberries from Sidhu Farms, Puyallup River Valley. Three-component blend: spelt saison (March 2024, aged in acacia wood) + spelt and wheat saisons (April and December 2024, aged in neutral oak). Bottle conditioned with organic sugar.

Brewer note (from Untappd/bottle log): "This is young-ish in the bottle and will continue to improve for the next few months if you keep it at room temperature. Should be at its best June-October 2026, drink by summer 2028."

Sources:
[Untappd - Ill Fate (2025 Harvest)](https://untappd.com/b/floodland-brewing-ill-fate-2025-harvest/6641155)
[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)
food_pairings: Fresh raspberry desserts, aged chèvre, duck confit, charcuterie with fruit preserves, dark chocolate
considerations: Very young — bottled Nov 2025, just ~5 months old. Best enjoyed after June 2026 per brewer. Bottle conditioned, expect light sediment. Acacia wood aging is unusual and adds a subtle honeyed, almost floral wood note not found in neutral oak beers.

name: Winesap
research:
From Untappd / Floodland: barrel-aged saison blend with organic Winesap apples from Filaree Fruit (Okanogan Valley, WA). Milled and pressed apples fermented in barrel with aged spelt saison, then aged through winter and spring. Bottled 07/10/2025 with organic sugar conditioning.

Brewery note: "Won't peak for at least a year... fall 2026. Should drink well until at least 2028 if not longer."

[Floodland Brewing Bottle Log](https://www.floodlandbrewing.com/bottlelog/)

name: Saint Lamvinus
research:
Untappd: "Maceration of different grape varieties (merlot, grenache noir, syrah) in two-year-old lambic. Beer with a taste evolution. Bottled 7 November 2023."

Cantillon Saint Lamvinus is one of the brewery's most sought-after releases — a lambic refermented on red wine grapes. The grape tannins and acidity interplay with the lambic character over years of bottle conditioning. High ABV (7.5%) and grape content support long aging.

Rating: 4.28/5 (2,232 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brasserie-cantillon-saint-lamvinus-2023/5637350)
food_pairings: Aged red wine cheese (Comté, Manchego), charcuterie, duck, venison. The vinous character pairs beautifully with food that normally accompanies red wine.
considerations: One of Cantillon's most complex and age-worthy releases. The 2023 was bottled November 2023 — recommend allowing 3 years before opening (fall 2026 or later). No longer in production.

name: Saint Lamvinus
research:
Untappd: 2024 vintage of Cantillon's flagship grape lambic — maceration of red wine grapes (merlot, grenache noir, syrah) in two-year-old lambic. Reviewers note it "could use a bit more time" — appropriate for a young vintage. Rated 4.21/5 (391 ratings).

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brasserie-cantillon-saint-lamvinus-2024-draft-version/6348869)
food_pairings: Aged red wine cheese, charcuterie, duck, venison.
considerations: Younger than the 2023 — allow more bottle time. Community reviews explicitly suggest not rushing this one. Expect peak around 2027-2030.

name: Sang Bleu
research:
Untappd: previously known as "Camerise Lambic," rebranded as Sang Bleu (French for "Blue Blood") with new artwork by artist Ammo. A lambic blend with haskap (blue honeysuckle) berries. Brewer: "powerful and very fruit-forward, but still maintains a nice, mellow balance between acidity and astringency."

Rating: 4.21/5 (2,418 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brasserie-cantillon-sang-bleu-2025/6217278)
food_pairings: Blue cheese, duck breast, lamb, dark chocolate. The haskap berry acidity plays well with rich, savory flavors.
considerations: Haskap (blue honeysuckle) is relatively unusual in lambic production — expect blueberry and dark berry notes with good acidity. The rebranding from Camerise Lambic is cosmetic. 2025 vintage — allow 2 years before opening.

name: Magic Lambic
research:
Untappd: Lambic - Framboise (raspberry lambic) from Cantillon. The 2025 vintage. Rated 4.32/5 (highly regarded). Traditional Cantillon raspberry lambic — spontaneous fermentation with whole raspberries.

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brasserie-cantillon-magic-lambic-2025/6248244)
food_pairings: Dark chocolate, raspberry tart, soft cheeses. Classic framboise pairings.
considerations: Cantillon's framboise program. Magic Lambic is one of their more fruit-forward releases. 2025 vintage — allow ~2 years before opening.

name: Ashanti
research:
Untappd: "2025 Vintage of the Gorilla/Ashanti/Guinee pepper lambic." A Cantillon specialty using Ashanti/Guinee pepper (Piper guineense) — an African pepper with warm, woody, aromatic spice character distinct from black pepper.

Rating: 4.31/5 (1,258 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/brasserie-cantillon-ashanti-2025/6357135)
food_pairings: Spiced dishes, grilled meats, aged Gouda. The pepper character pairs with savory, warming food.
considerations: Ashanti pepper (Piper guineense) — also known as West African pepper or Benin pepper — gives warm, peppery, slightly woody aromatics. 2025 vintage. Allow ~2 years before opening. One of Cantillon's more unusual specialty releases.

name: Oude Kriek
research:
Untappd: traditional lambic Kriek using Schaarbeekse cherries — the rare sour morello variety prized for kriek production. Described as "raspberry-like Schaarbeekse Kriek" with "sweet-tart blackberry depth" and "perfect acidity/complexity balance."

Rating: 4.12/5 (2,172 ratings)

[Untappd listing](https://untappd.com/b/geuzestekerij-de-cam-oude-kriek/66369)
food_pairings: Dark chocolate, duck, venison, cherry-glazed pork. The kriek acidity loves rich, game-forward dishes.
considerations: Best-before date printed on bottle: 12/10/2034. De Cam is a traditional Pajottenland blending house (geuzestekerij) — they blend and age lambic from other producers. Schaarbeekse cherries are extremely rare and valued for their high acidity and complex flavor.
